assets.modifications: Fifteen generated clips. Startup, 22.05 kHz: boom (0.5 s), small boom (0.3 s), clank (40 ms), thud (80 ms), hum loop (1.0 s), klaxon (three 120 ms square chirps, 0.5 s), servo loop (1.2 kHz sine with a 6 Hz vibrato, 1.0 s), winch loop (90 Hz saw with a 7 Hz wobble, 1.0 s), whine (sine sweep 300 Hz to 1.8 kHz, 0.6 s) and, added 2026-10-13 in an AI-assisted pass (Claude Code) and not yet picked by ear, chirp (two soft sine blips a fifth apart, 1.32 kHz then 1.98 kHz, 0.15 s) and actuator (a low-passed saw gliding 150 to 230 Hz and back with a 38 Hz gear ripple, 0.24 s); both are pure tones that draw nothing from the seeded noise, so the earlier clips keep their bytes. Detailed, 44.1 kHz (added 2026-10-10): relay_spark (recipe A: snap, 120 Hz pulsing buzz and crackle, 0.34 s), records_arc (recipe B: N-wave crack, short housing knock, restrike, pulsing tail with the late crackle faded out, 0.65 s), bolt_arc (recipe B: 0.5 s build of buzz and crackle, then the crack and restrike, 0.8 s) and growl_warning (recipe C: chaotic subharmonic throat in a metal chassis with a wandering swell and two snarl bursts, 1.2 s). Retired 2026-10-10: the generated hiss loop, arc crackle and growl (replaced by the recordings and the detailed recipes). Played through AudioStreamPlayer nodes on the Effects bus; volume and pitch are set per use.

assets.source_reference: Supplied by Nathanial Henniges on 2026-10-12 for the studio logo screen; rsvg-convert 2.63.2 (librsvg, cairo 1.18.6): `rsvg-convert -w 702 -h 702 <svg> -o <png>`. Chosen after comparing against macOS QuickLook previews (`qlmanage -t -s 1024`, which matches the supplied previews pixel for pixel but renders on opaque white): at 1024 px rsvg-convert differed by 0.18-0.24% RMSE, Godot 4.7.2 Image.load_svg_from_buffer (ThorVG) by 0.39-0.44% and ImageMagick 7.1.2's internal MSVG renderer by 19.5% (it dropped most fills), so rsvg-convert is the most faithful renderer that keeps transparency.

assets.modifications: Rendered from the closed-mouth SVG at 702x702 px, then trimmed to the bounds both mascot SVGs share (288x600+192+45) with Pillow 12.3 and NumPy 2.5, so the smirk and the grin line up pixel for pixel. 288x600 RGBA, 90,175 B; imported with mipmaps (shown at 144x300 in the 960x540 view, so 1:1 at 1080p and on a 1080-pixel-high phone).
assets.implementation_status: In use since 2026-10-12 as the mascot on the studio logo screen (scenes/studio_logo.tscn Mascot), the game's first scene.

assets.modifications: The grin is drawn as a patch over the smirk. Both SVGs rendered at 702x702 and trimmed to the same 288x600 bounds; the open-mouth render differs from the smirk by more than 25% only around the mouth (elsewhere at most 24/255, sub-pixel outline offsets between the two files), so the grin frame takes the open-mouth pixels inside a 112x68 box at (64, 180) on a 4 px grid, blended over 3 px towards its edge and equal to the smirk on its 1 px outer ring, and keeps the smirk everywhere else. Every patch pixel is opaque, so drawing it over the smirk gives that grin frame exactly; the composed grin differs from the smirk in 2,703 pixels, all inside the box. 112x68 RGBA, 7,554 B; imported with mipmaps.
